facts.label: Document-level observations bearing on downstream use
facts.text: - Maturity schedule: the 10-K principal payments table (page:86) is stated as of December 31, 2025 and carries the European facility at its earlier maturity. The Q2 10-Q (page:11, page:42) states the extension from November 23, 2027 to April 30, 2031 and that principal payments on borrowings run from February 2028 through September 2032, apart from quarterly term loan payments. For June 30, 2026 maturity work, the Q2 10-Q controls and the 10-K table must not be reused unadjusted. - Covenant terms: the 10-K prints covenant tests per facility (page:87 to page:89), including a maximum ERC ratio of 45% on the European facility. The Q2 10-Q (page:11) states that the amendment reduced it to 40%. The Q2 10-Q confirms compliance as of June 30, 2026 (page:11, page:42) but prints no actual ratio level, and refers to the 10-K for facility detail. The Q1 10-Q (page:17) lists the changes "among other modifications" and says the aggregate revolving borrowings available and funding costs remained unchanged. Whether other European covenant terms changed on amendment is not verifiable without the amended agreement, which the Q2 10-Q lists as Exhibit 10.1 filed with that report (page:48) and which is not supplied. - Availability: availability is printed by facility at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:54), March 31, 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:32) and June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:40 and page:41). It is split into an amount based on current ERC and an additional amount subject to borrowing base and advance rates. Availability is therefore tied to ERC and to the borrowing base definitions, which are not supplied in full. - ERC: the European ERC step-up is $348.5 million per the Q2 10-Q (page:24) and approximately $349 million per the Q2 release (page:1), a rounding difference. The Q2 10-Q (page:9) states the positive adjustment to changes in expected future recoveries from the European forecast update was approximately $105 million, with partial offsets in other pools; the total positive adjustment to changes in expected future recoveries for the quarter is $74.2 million (page:9). Headline ERC change and income effect are different measures, and a consumer must carry both. - Non-GAAP: Adjusted EBITDA is printed by the issuer for the last twelve months ended June 30, 2026 and for fiscal 2025 (Q2 release page:11), and its definition adds back recoveries collected and applied to finance receivables less changes in expected recoveries. It is a management non-GAAP measure, labelled as such in the 10-Q (page:24, page:35). The Q2 10-Q key metrics table (page:25) prints the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA for both periods behind the stated 9.6% increase; the Q2 release reconciliation (page:11) prints the June 30, 2026 last-twelve-months and fiscal 2025 columns only, so the prior-year reconciliation is not supplied. - Goodwill: a goodwill impairment of $412,611 thousand is recorded in the quarter ended September 30, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:3) and carries into fiscal 2025 and the last twelve months. Net loss labels in the Adjusted EBITDA table (Q2 release page:11) refer to those long periods and not to the positive Q2 2026 quarter. - Legal: the 10-K describes a multi-state Attorneys General investigation open since November 17, 2015 and an accrual for an estimated loss on that matter (page:102 and page:103). The Q2 10-Q states no material developments (page:17). The accrued amount is not stated in those pages.

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported base is complete for the audited year ended December 31, 2025, the comparative year 2024 and the interim periods to June 30, 2026. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, gross debt (credit facilities plus senior notes, at principal) was $3,771.3 million at June 30, 2026 against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of $1,358.9 million, which is 2.78x gross and 2.68x after deducting cash and cash equivalents of $132.4 million. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 5.36x. facts.label: Credit read-through
facts.text: - Leverage trend. Gross debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 2.93x at FY2024, 2.82x at FY2025 and 2.78x for the last twelve months to June 30, 2026. Debt principal rose 13.0% from FY2024 to June 30, 2026 while Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.5%, so the ratio fell. The mechanism is higher collections on recently purchased portfolios (cash collections of 2,107,626 in FY2025 against 1,868,576 in FY2024) and a larger ERC (8,894,515 at June 30, 2026), financed with debt. - Funding gap. Adjusted EBITDA after cash interest and cash taxes was less than cash spent on portfolio purchases and capital expenditure in FY2025 and FY2024 (bridge in Calculations). Borrowings at carrying value rose from 2,914,270 at December 31, 2023 to 3,326,621 and then 3,697,338 (10-K page:39) and net debt cash flows were positive in both years (C8), so leverage is a function of purchase volume. Management states it can slow purchases "without significantly impacting current year collections" (10-K page:55); that is a management statement, not evidenced by the supplied tables. - Earnings quality. In Q2 2026 changes in expected recoveries were 96,924 of income from operations of 153,282, driven by the European forecast revision. These are estimates of future collections recognised in income now; Portfolio income, which the filing calls the more predictable yield component, was 267,799 (Q2 10-Q page:29). Cash collections of 558,545 are the stronger measure of performance in the quarter. - Liquidity. Cash is 132,431 against total availability of 998,468, of which 733,096 is based on current ERC. Availability moved from 1,099,466 at December 31, 2025 to 998,468 at June 30, 2026 as revolver drawings rose; the supplied text does not give letters of credit drawn. - Maturities. After the April 2026 extension no principal other than the term loan's quarterly payments falls due before February 2028 (Q2 10-Q page:42). The 2029 concentration is the largest, with both revolvers, the 2029 notes and the term loan balance maturing in October 2029. - Interest. Interest expense, net was 251,788 in FY2025 (cash interest paid 259,061) and 127,881 in H1 2026. Interest expense, net rose 3.2% year on year in Q2 2026, which the filing attributes primarily to higher average debt balances (Q2 10-Q page:32).

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: PRA Group, Inc. is a Delaware specialty finance company headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia that buys nonperforming consumer loans from banks, consumer finance companies, auto finance providers and other creditors, and collects on them over several years through call centers, external vendors, legal recovery and digital channels (10-K page:6 to page:8). It reports two segments, the U.S. and Europe, created in Q4 2025 after a new chief executive officer was appointed in 2025 (10-K page:103), plus smaller operations in South America, Canada and Australia. Revenue is accrued from the expected collections of each portfolio, so reported profit depends on management's collection forecasts; the filing itself calls Portfolio income the more predictable component and Changes in expected recoveries the estimate-driven one (Q2 10-Q page:29). The company is publicly listed with 44 holders of record and no sponsor, parent or controlling holder is disclosed in the supplied sources; the proxy statement that would give beneficial ownership is not supplied. No acquisition, take-private or other ownership transaction is described in the supplied sources. The transactions that are described are financing and portfolio events: the September 30, 2025 issue of euro-denominated 6.250% senior notes due 2032 by a Luxembourg subsidiary, the April 30, 2026 amendment and extension of the European revolving credit facility, the April 2025 sale of an 11.7% interest in a Brazilian servicing company, and the August 3, 2026 approval of a new share repurchase program. Creditor-relevant change is concentrated in three areas: the June 30, 2026 European forecast review that raised European ERC by $348.5 million; the cost and organisation programme under the "PRA 3.0" strategy (management's term); and capital returns through repurchases while portfolio purchases are financed with debt. Documented actions show no priming, uptiering, drop-down or related-party leakage, but the legal capacity under the credit agreements and indentures cannot be assessed because those documents are not supplied.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: No acquisition, take-private, merger or other ownership transaction is described in the supplied sources, and the context holds no deal terms, so the transaction view is Insufficient Information for any pending or announced ownership event as of 2026-11-05; the sources end on August 7, 2026. The financing and portfolio transactions that are described are as follows. On September 30, 2025 the company completed a private offering of EUR 300.0 million (US$352.4 million at issuance) of 6.250% senior notes due September 30, 2032 through its wholly owned subsidiary PRA Group Europe Holding II S.à r.l.; the notes are senior unsecured obligations of that issuer, guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by PRA Group, Inc. and by the domestic restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the North American facility, with interest payable on March 31 and September 30, a change of control put at 101%, and a call schedule at 103.125% from September 30, 2028 falling to par from 2030 (10-K page:90). The use of proceeds is not stated in the pages read, so it is Insufficient Information; the cash flow statement shows the proceeds within financing activities (10-K page:71) and the company describes the issue as its first euro-denominated senior notes (10-K page:38). On April 30, 2026 the company amended and restated its European revolving credit facility: the maturity moved from November 23, 2027 to April 30, 2031, the maximum ERC ratio fell from 45.0% to 40.0%, and, subject to conditions, borrowers may make investments in or loans to joint ventures up to EUR 100 million; the Q1 2026 10-Q reports the aggregate revolving borrowings available and funding costs as unchanged (Q1 10-Q page:17; Q2 10-Q page:11). The joint venture basket is a new permission that could move value outside the borrower group, but its use is not evidenced and the agreement is not supplied. Earlier debt history inside the sources: in 2024 the company issued 8.875% senior notes due January 31, 2030 ($400.0 million on May 20, 2024 and a further $150.0 million on November 25, 2024 at 103.625% of principal) and retired 2025 senior notes (10-K page:91; Q3 10-Q page:6; 10-K page:71). Other events: the April 2025 sale of the 11.7% interest in RCB Investimentos S.A. with a gain of $38.4 million, stated not to affect ownership of the portfolio investments in South America (10-K page:43); the Q3 2025 goodwill impairment, recognised after a quantitative test that compared fair value with market capitalization (Q3 10-Q page:12); and, as a subsequent event to the June 30, 2026 balance sheet, the August 3, 2026 board approval of a new share repurchase program of up to $150 million, subject to covenants and board discretion (Q2 10-Q page:21). The new program follows repurchases of $20.0 million in 2025 and $20.0 million in the first half of 2026 (10-K page:38; Q2 10-Q page:15). Amounts of each financing and the debt table are in the CP-1 handoff.

Earlier debt history inside the sources: in 2024 the company issued 8.875% senior notes due January 31, 2030 ($400.0 million on May 20, 2024 and a further $150.0 million on November 25, 2024 at 103.625% of principal) and retired 2025 senior notes (10-K page:91; Q3 10-Q page:6; 10-K page:71). Other events: the April 2025 sale of the 11.7% interest in RCB Investimentos S.A. with a gain of $38.4 million, stated not to affect ownership of the portfolio investments in South America (10-K page:43); the Q3 2025 goodwill impairment, recognised after a quantitative test that compared fair value with market capitalization (Q3 10-Q page:12); and, as a subsequent event to the June 30, 2026 balance sheet, the August 3, 2026 board approval of a new share repurchase program of up to $150 million, subject to covenants and board discretion (Q2 10-Q page:21). The new program follows repurchases of $20.0 million in 2025 and $20.0 million in the first half of 2026 (10-K page:38; Q2 10-Q page:15). facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: PRA Group's fundamental credit is adequate and stable, with moderate leverage that depends on forecast accuracy more than on a cash buffer. The strongest support is cash earning power: last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,358.9 million covers cash interest of USD 253.4 million 5.36x, gross debt is 2.78x that EBITDA, and no principal other than term loan payments is due before February 2028. The weakest point is that revenue, ERC and ERC-linked availability of USD 998.5 million all rest on internal collection forecasts, while purchases have exceeded post-interest cash earnings in each of the last two years. What decides the outcome is whether collections keep matching forecasts and whether purchasing is held to the cash the business generates. Covenant headroom cannot be observed.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, the leverage and coverage position is moderate and has improved. Gross debt over Adjusted EBITDA was 2.93x in FY2024 and 2.78x for the last twelve months to June 30, 2026, because between FY2024 and the last twelve months to June 30, 2026 Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.5% while debt principal rose 13.0%. Cash interest cover was 5.08x in FY2025 and 5.36x for the last twelve months [CP-1 leverage and interest cover tables]. The measure is the issuer's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back collections applied to principal, so it is a cash-collections measure and is not the covenant definition; ratios should not be compared with the 3.50x and 2.50x limits.

The USD 348.5 million is an ERC change and not income. Cash collections of USD 558.5 million in the quarter are the firmer measure.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The company has a long-dated, diversified liability stack: secured revolving facilities in several currencies, a term loan and unsecured notes, with no principal beyond term loan payments due for about 15 months and revolvers running to 2029 and 2031. Cash earning power is growing: cash collections of USD 558.5 million in Q2 2026 are 4.2% above Q2 2025, ERC is USD 8,894.5 million, 2.36x debt principal, and Adjusted EBITDA has risen 9.6% year on year. Purchasing is discretionary, which gives management a lever over debt growth. The European business is organised so that portfolio ownership and collections sit in the same entity, and the European and UK facilities are multi-currency to match funding by currency (10-K page:65). The company is widely held, with no sponsor, no dividends in three years and a documented early extension of its European facility, and it discloses reconciliations of its non-GAAP measures and ERC revisions.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Earnings, ERC and the ERC-based part of availability depend on internal models and forecasts, and a USD 412.6 million goodwill impairment in Q3 2025 shows that valuations can reset sharply. Cash on hand is small, USD 132.4 million against USD 3,771.3 million of debt, so liquidity is a function of revolver access and covenant compliance, which cannot be observed. Debt has grown faster than cash after purchases in two consecutive years, and shareholder returns continue through repurchases, with a USD 150 million program approved on August 3, 2026. Europe is 54.0% of ERC, adding currency and fragmented regulatory exposure, and the U.S. segment's adjusted operating income was flat year on year in Q2 2026 as legal collection spending rose. A multi-state Attorneys General investigation open since 2015 remains unresolved. The 2029 maturity cluster and the structural position of unsecured noteholders behind secured facilities add refinancing and ranking sensitivity.

facts.text: - K1, maturity concentration: 2029 principal 1,837,149 / 3,771,251 = 48.7%. Principal due by end-2028: 5,000 + 10,000 + 408,245 = 423,245; 423,245 / 3,771,251 = 11.2%. The 2028 notes mature on February 1, 2028, 453 days after the as-of date of 2026-11-05 (about 14.9 months); the October 28, 2029 revolver maturity is 1,088 days after it (about 3.0 years). - K2, secured share: credit facility borrowings 2,130,621 / 3,771,251 = 56.5%; senior notes 1,640,630 / 3,771,251 = 43.5%. Whether the Colombian facility (245) is secured is not stated and is immaterial to the share. - K3, ERC-based share of availability: 733,096 / 998,468 = 73.4%. - K4, liquidity cover of the next 12 months: cash 132,431 + availability 998,468 = 1,130,899; divided by the printed estimate of interest, unused fees and principal payments for the next 12 months of 247,700 (Q2 10-Q page:42) = 4.57x. Availability alone: 998,468 / 247,700 = 4.03x. Letters of credit drawn are Not supplied, so no deduction is made. - K5, interest rate sensitivity: 7,800 / 253,430 (cash interest, CP-1 C4) = 3.1% of cash interest per 50 basis points, on the company's estimate (Q2 10-Q page:46). - K6, illustrative cost-adjusted ERC cover (analyst construct, not an issuer measure): ERC 8,894,515 x Q2 2026 cash efficiency ratio 61.2% (Q2 10-Q page:25) = 5,443,443; divided by debt principal 3,771,251 = 1.44x. #### Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 (`10-Q_2025-09-30_praa-20250930.htm.jsonl`)
- Family and authority: filed quarterly report, unaudited. page:1 "For the quarterly period ended September 30, 2025".

- Statements: balance sheet page:2, income statement page:3 (three and nine months), cash flows page:6. Note 5 Borrowings page:12 and page:13. Goodwill impairment of the quarter at page:3 and page:12. Segments Note 12 at page:20. Liquidity at page:42 and page:43.

- Signature date not visible in the extracted text (page:52 shows only the officer title). This does not affect period identification, which rests on page:1.
#### Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 (`10-Q_2026-03-31_praa-20260331.htm.jsonl`)
- Family and authority: filed quarterly report, unaudited, signed May 8, 2026 (page:40). page:1 "For the quarterly period ended March 31, 2026".

- Statements: balance sheet page:2, income statement page:3, cash flows page:4 and page:5. Note 5 Borrowings page:8 and page:9. Liquidity page:32 and page:33. ERC page:28. Segments Note 13 page:14 and page:15.

- Note 15 Subsequent Event (page:17): the European revolving credit facility was amended and restated on April 30, 2026. The Note 5 text on page:9 still gives the earlier maturity and refers forward to this amendment, so the two statements are one dated sequence and not a conflict.
#### Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 (`10-Q_2026-06-30_praa-20260630.htm.jsonl`)

- Family and authority: filed quarterly report, unaudited, signed August 7, 2026 (page:49). page:1 "For the quarterly period ended June 30, 2026". Shares outstanding as of July 31, 2026 are on the cover.

- Statements: balance sheet page:2, income statement page:3 (three and six months with 2025 comparatives), equity page:4, cash flows page:5 (six months, with cash paid for interest and taxes). Units "(in thousands)". USD.

- Debt: Note 5 Borrowings at page:11, giving credit facility borrowings, each senior note series and the amended European facility terms. Liquidity and availability by facility at page:40 and page:41; borrowings and 12-month cash obligations at page:42.

- Other: Note 2 finance receivables and changes in expected recoveries (page:7 to page:10), derivatives (page:12), commitments (page:17), segments Note 13 (page:17 to page:19), Note 15 subsequent event (page:21), non-GAAP and ERC tables (page:35 to page:40), exhibit index (page:47 and page:48).
- Role: most recent filed statements in the pack and the controlling source for June 30, 2026 balances and for the post-amendment European facility terms stated in the filing.
#### Earnings releases (Exhibit 99.1)

- Q4 and full year 2025, February 26, 2026: headline results page:1, cash collections and purchases by source page:3 and page:4, income statement page:5 and page:6, Adjusted EBITDA and net income reconciliations page:11 and page:12. The release is dated before the 10-K audit report (March 2, 2026), so the 10-K controls for annual statement facts.
- Q1 2026, May 7, 2026: headline results page:1, reconciliations page:10 and page:11. The 10-Q for the same quarter controls for statement facts.

- Q2 2026, August 6, 2026: headline results page:1 to page:3, credit availability page:3, share repurchase page:4, statements page:6 and page:7, Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation for the last twelve months and fiscal 2025 at page:11. The 10-Q controls for statement facts.

- Authority: issuer-prepared, unaudited, furnished. They support attributed management narrative, non-GAAP measures and cash collections and purchases by source. They do not override a filing. They are not independent corroboration of figures that repeat the filings.
### Information-availability boundary and version relationships
- Latest dated source: the Q2 2026 10-Q signed August 7, 2026; the Q2 release is dated August 6, 2026. The as-of date and cutoff are 2026-11-05.

- Nothing dated between August 7, 2026 and the cutoff is supplied. Any 8-K, any report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and any financing or rating event in that window are Not supplied. That is not evidence that none exists.

- Subsequent events inside the pack: April 30, 2026 European facility amendment (Q1 10-Q page:17, Q2 10-Q page:11 and page:42) and the August 3, 2026 board approval of a new $150 million share repurchase program (Q2 10-Q page:21, Q2 release page:4).

- Each release and its same-period filing overlap. Retained for statement facts: the filing. Retained for non-GAAP measures not defined in the filing and for cash collections by source: the release, attributed to management.
- Q2 2025 as a discrete reporting period is not supplied as a filing; its comparatives appear in the Q2 2026 10-Q (three and six months columns, page:3) and the Q2 2026 release.

- Comparatives for December 31, 2025 appear in the Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs and in the 10-K. Whether any comparative was re-presented between filings has not been tested in CP-0; consumers must compare the same balance across the filings that print it.

- Segments: the 10-K states the business was reorganized from a single operating segment into U.S. and European reportable segments in Q4 2025 and that prior-year disclosures were recast (page:103 and page:104). The Q3 2025 10-Q segment note (page:20) states a single operating segment, so it predates that change, so 2025 segment data differs by basis across filings.
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: PRA Group, Inc., consolidated with subsidiaries and noncontrolling interests (balance sheet and income statement, Q2 10-Q page:2 and page:3). The context leaves borrower, parent and guarantor fields blank; that is not evidence they are absent.

- Debt instruments and parties as printed: North American credit facility (revolving and term loan) guaranteed by U.S. and Canadian subsidiaries and secured by a first priority lien on substantially all assets (10-K page:87); UK revolving credit facility secured by PRA Group UK Limited assets and certain equity interests (10-K page:88); European revolving credit facility, guaranteed by the Company, secured by equity interests in operating subsidiaries of the named borrowers (10-K page:89); 2028, 2029 and 2030 senior notes issued by the Company with guarantees from domestic restricted subsidiaries (10-K page:90 to page:92); 2032 senior notes issued by PRA Group Europe Holding II S.à r.l. and guaranteed by the Company and domestic restricted subsidiaries (10-K page:90).

- Covenants are written on "the Company's consolidated" ratios (10-K page:87 to page:89). The ratio definitions, the restricted group and any unrestricted subsidiaries are not in the supplied text. Treat as unresolved.

- Currency and units: statements and releases are USD in thousands; the 10-K MD&A and 10-Q MD&A text use millions. Europe is 54.0% of June 30, 2026 ERC (Q2 10-Q page:24) and non-U.S. amounts are translated (for example the 2032 senior notes are denominated in euro, EUR 300.0 million at issuance, 10-K page:90, and shown in USD in the borrowings tables). Constant-currency tables appear in the releases (Q2 release page:2). Balances move with exchange rates.
- Draft versus executed: all supplied documents are filed. No agreement, indenture or amendment is supplied, so no executed-versus-draft question arises for legal terms; they are simply absent.
### Document-level observations bearing on downstream use

- Maturity schedule: the 10-K principal payments table (page:86) is stated as of December 31, 2025 and carries the European facility at its earlier maturity. The Q2 10-Q (page:11, page:42) states the extension from November 23, 2027 to April 30, 2031 and that principal payments on borrowings run from February 2028 through September 2032, apart from quarterly term loan payments. For June 30, 2026 maturity work, the Q2 10-Q controls and the 10-K table must not be reused unadjusted.

- Covenant terms: the 10-K prints covenant tests per facility (page:87 to page:89), including a maximum ERC ratio of 45% on the European facility. The Q2 10-Q (page:11) states that the amendment reduced it to 40%. The Q2 10-Q confirms compliance as of June 30, 2026 (page:11, page:42) but prints no actual ratio level, and refers to the 10-K for facility detail. The Q1 10-Q (page:17) lists the changes "among other modifications" and says the aggregate revolving borrowings available and funding costs remained unchanged. Whether other European covenant terms changed on amendment is not verifiable without the amended agreement, which the Q2 10-Q lists as Exhibit 10.1 filed with that report (page:48) and which is not supplied.

- Availability: availability is printed by facility at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:54), March 31, 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:32) and June 30, 2026 (Q2 10-Q page:40 and page:41). It is split into an amount based on current ERC and an additional amount subject to borrowing base and advance rates. Availability is therefore tied to ERC and to the borrowing base definitions, which are not supplied in full.

- ERC: the European ERC step-up is $348.5 million per the Q2 10-Q (page:24) and approximately $349 million per the Q2 release (page:1), a rounding difference. The Q2 10-Q (page:9) states the positive adjustment to changes in expected future recoveries from the European forecast update was approximately $105 million, with partial offsets in other pools; the total positive adjustment to changes in expected future recoveries for the quarter is $74.2 million (page:9). Headline ERC change and income effect are different measures, and a consumer must carry both.

- Non-GAAP: Adjusted EBITDA is printed by the issuer for the last twelve months ended June 30, 2026 and for fiscal 2025 (Q2 release page:11), and its definition adds back recoveries collected and applied to finance receivables less changes in expected recoveries. It is a management non-GAAP measure, labelled as such in the 10-Q (page:24, page:35). The Q2 10-Q key metrics table (page:25) prints the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA for both periods behind the stated 9.6% increase; the Q2 release reconciliation (page:11) prints the June 30, 2026 last-twelve-months and fiscal 2025 columns only, so the prior-year reconciliation is not supplied.

- Goodwill: a goodwill impairment of $412,611 thousand is recorded in the quarter ended September 30, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:3) and carries into fiscal 2025 and the last twelve months. Net loss labels in the Adjusted EBITDA table (Q2 release page:11) refer to those long periods and not to the positive Q2 2026 quarter.

- Legal: the 10-K describes a multi-state Attorneys General investigation open since November 17, 2015 and an accrual for an estimated loss on that matter (page:102 and page:103). The Q2 10-Q states no material developments (page:17). The accrued amount is not stated in those pages.
### Consumer evidence demand
| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, notes, debt by facility, cash paid for interest, segments, non-GAAP | 10-K page:68 to page:71, page:86 to page:92, page:103 to page:105; Q3 10-Q page:2 to page:6, page:12; Q1 10-Q page:2 to page:5, page:8; Q2 10-Q page:2 to page:5, page:11, page:17 to page:19; releases page:6 and page:11 | Cash flows in the 10-Qs are year-to-date, so a discrete quarter is a derivation from two supplied statements. Segment basis changed in Q4 2025. Text conversion flattens tables. |

| CP-1A | Business model, segments, strategy, management and governance, capital allocation, transactions | 10-K page:6 to page:15, page:35, page:96; Q2 10-Q page:24, page:25, page:42, page:43; Q2 release page:1 to page:4 | Proxy statement (governance and ownership) not supplied. 8-K filings that the exhibit index cites are not supplied. |

| CP-2 | Handoffs from CP-1 and CP-1A, plus covenants, availability, maturities, ERC, lease and commitment text | 10-K page:50 to page:57, page:86 to page:92; Q2 10-Q page:11, page:36 to page:42 | Executed agreements, covenant calculations, ratings, market prices and peers not supplied. |
| CP-5 | Traceable locators for every claim | All seven sources carry page locators | Rendering, charts, original HTML and XBRL cannot be inspected; the check is of text only. |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: seven filed or furnished documents, every page retained, cover the audited year ended December 31, 2025 and interim periods to June 30, 2026. Facility-level borrowings, availability and senior note terms are printed for December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026, with March 31, 2026 in the Q1 10-Q. Cash paid for interest is printed in the 10-K and the 2026 10-Qs.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the covenants and the borrowing base depend on definitions in agreements that are not supplied, and the European facility was amended after the 10-K. The filings assert compliance but print no ratio levels, so headroom is not observable in the sources.

- Source risk mechanism: availability is partly "based on current ERC" and ERC rose by $348.5 million through a forecast revision in the quarter ended June 30, 2026. A consumer that treats ERC-based availability or the earnings effect as equally firm as cash collected would overstate certainty, because the revision is a management estimate (Q2 10-Q page:9).

- What cannot proceed: covenant headroom against agreement definitions, guarantor-level analysis, legal terms of the notes beyond the 10-K summaries, ratings analysis, valuation against market prices, and any assessment of events after August 7, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the Second Amended and Restated European credit agreement (Q2 10-Q Exhibit 10.1), the North American and UK credit agreements, the four indentures listed at Q2 10-Q page:48, any 8-K filed after the Q2 10-Q, and any report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 that exists before the cutoff.
## Calculations

No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Every figure above is quoted as printed in the cited page, and the stated rounding relationship between $348.5 million and approximately $349 million is the issuer's own.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Remediation |

| Amended European revolving credit agreement and the other credit agreements not supplied | High for legal and covenant work; Medium for synthesis | CP-2 | Supply Exhibit 10.1 of the Q2 10-Q and the North American and UK agreements |
| Indentures for the 2028, 2029, 2030 and 2032 senior notes not supplied | Medium | CP-2 | Supply the four indentures listed at Q2 10-Q page:48 |
| Actual covenant ratio levels not printed; only compliance statements | High | CP-2 | Supply compliance certificates or issuer disclosure of ratio levels; otherwise keep Not supplied |
| Covenant and borrowing base definitions (consolidated EBITDA, fixed charge coverage, ERC ratio, restricted group) not supplied | High | CP-2 | Supply the executed agreements |

| Events after August 7, 2026 (8-Ks, the report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 if filed, financing, rating actions) not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply later filings or confirm none |

| Q2 2025 filing and the prior-year last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation not supplied (only the metric is printed, Q2 10-Q page:25) | Low | CP-1 | Use the comparatives in the Q2 2026 10-Q; do not build the prior reconciliation |
| Proxy statement for the 2026 annual meeting (Part III, governance, ownership) not supplied | Low | CP-1A | Supply if governance detail is needed |
| Quarterly earnings presentation slides referenced by the Q2 release not supplied | Low | CP-1A | Not required for the selected scope |
| No credit ratings, market prices, peer data or valuation inputs | Low for the selected modules | CP-2 | Keep Not supplied; context fields are blank |

| Accrued amount for the multi-state Attorneys General matter not stated in the 10-K contingencies note (page:102 and page:103) | Low to Medium | CP-2 | Keep Not supplied unless a supplied source states it |
| Text conversions only; original HTML, XBRL and charts not supplied | Low | CP-1, CP-5 | Check flagged tables against the filed HTML when available |
| Segment basis differs across 2025 filings (single segment before Q4 2025) | Medium | CP-1 | Use recast comparatives in the 2026 filings and label the basis |
## Next module

- CP-1: use the 10-K and the 10-Qs as controlling for statement facts; keep annual, quarterly and year-to-date columns separate; keep credit facility borrowings, each senior note series and unamortized premium and issuance costs separate; use the Q2 10-Q for June 30, 2026 maturities of the European facility and not the 10-K principal payment table; label the Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted net income and cash efficiency measures as issuer non-GAAP.

- CP-1A: carry the April 30, 2026 European facility amendment, the Q4 2025 segment reorganization, the PRA 3.0 strategy and the August 3, 2026 buyback authorization as dated events; label anything after August 7, 2026 as Not supplied.

- CP-2 and CP-5: carry the missing executed agreements, the missing covenant ratio levels and the difference between the $348.5 million ERC step-up and its approximately $105 million forecast-line effect as restrictions; do not present compliance statements as measured headroom.

### Financial base view

The reported base is complete for the audited year ended December 31, 2025, the comparative year 2024 and the interim periods to June 30, 2026. On the issuer's own Adjusted EBITDA, gross debt (credit facilities plus senior notes, at principal) was $3,771.3 million at June 30, 2026 against last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of $1,358.9 million, which is 2.78x gross and 2.68x after deducting cash and cash equivalents of $132.4 million. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest paid 5.36x. Total availability under the credit facilities was $998.5 million, of which $733.1 million is based on current ERC and $265.4 million is subject to borrowing base and advance rates. Quarterly cash collections were $558.5 million in Q2 2026. Three features limit how far these numbers can be pushed. First, PRA's Adjusted EBITDA adds back recoveries collected and applied to finance receivables less changes in expected recoveries, so it is a cash-collections measure and is not comparable with a conventional EBITDA; it is also not the EBITDA defined in the credit agreements, which is not supplied. Second, net cash used in operating activities is negative in every year shown because collections applied to principal are classified in investing activities, so operating cash flow and a free cash flow built from it are not meaningful here. Third, Q2 2026 earnings include a European forecast revision: changes in expected recoveries were $96.9 million of income from operations of $153.3 million. The base does not support a covenant headroom conclusion: compliance is stated but no covenant ratio is printed.

### Definition and data-quality review

- Adjusted EBITDA definition. The issuer adds net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, so the measure is before the minority share; distributions to noncontrolling interests were 25,132 in FY2025 and 1,522 in H1 2026 (10-K page:71; Q2 10-Q page:5). It replaces changes in expected recoveries with "recoveries collected and applied to Finance receivables, net", which moves the measure from an accrual revenue basis to a cash basis (10-K page:45). It is not the covenant EBITDA; covenant definitions are Not supplied. Do not compare the computed ratios to the 3.50x total leverage or 2.50x senior secured leverage tests.

- Nearest cash cross-check. The issuer's cash receipts less Adjusted operating expenses for FY2025 was 1,298,123 (10-K page:46); Adjusted EBITDA is 1,315,474, a difference of 17,351 whose components are not itemized in the filing.

- Operating cash flow. Net cash used in operating activities is negative in FY2024 and FY2025 and for H1 2025 and H1 2026 because collections applied to principal (1,099,148 in FY2025) sit in investing activities (Q2 10-Q page:44). Free cash flow from operating cash flow is Not calculable on a meaningful basis; the bridge below uses the issuer's cash measure instead.

- Debt perimeter. Total debt here is principal of credit facilities and senior notes. It excludes interest-bearing deposits (100,460), lease liabilities (30,681) and derivative liabilities. A sensitivity including deposits is in Calculations.

- Cash perimeter. Cash and cash equivalents of 132,431 includes 119.1 million held by international operations with indefinitely reinvested earnings (Q2 10-Q page:40). Investments of 145,473 are held "to meet liquidity requirements for our banking subsidiary" (page:43) and are excluded from net debt.
- Foreign currency. The 2032 notes, the European facility and the UK facility are non-USD or multi-currency; principal moves with exchange rates (for example the 2032 notes at 352,350 and 342,630).
- Segment basis. Single-segment before Q4 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:20); two reportable segments from Q4 2025 with recast comparatives (10-K page:103 and page:104).

- Goodwill. 412,611 impaired in Q3 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:3 and page:12), leaving 26,871. FY2025 and the last twelve months to March 31, 2026 and June 30, 2026 net loss therefore reflect a non-cash charge that Adjusted EBITDA adds back.

- Subsequent events. April 30, 2026 amendment of the European facility (Q1 10-Q page:17); August 3, 2026 approval of a new share repurchase program of up to 150 million (Q2 10-Q page:21). Neither changes a balance in the statements reported here.
### Credit read-through

- Leverage trend. Gross debt over Adjusted EBITDA is 2.93x at FY2024, 2.82x at FY2025 and 2.78x for the last twelve months to June 30, 2026. Debt principal rose 13.0% from FY2024 to June 30, 2026 while Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.5%, so the ratio fell. The mechanism is higher collections on recently purchased portfolios (cash collections of 2,107,626 in FY2025 against 1,868,576 in FY2024) and a larger ERC (8,894,515 at June 30, 2026), financed with debt.

- Funding gap. Adjusted EBITDA after cash interest and cash taxes was less than cash spent on portfolio purchases and capital expenditure in FY2025 and FY2024 (bridge in Calculations). Borrowings at carrying value rose from 2,914,270 at December 31, 2023 to 3,326,621 and then 3,697,338 (10-K page:39) and net debt cash flows were positive in both years (C8), so leverage is a function of purchase volume. Management states it can slow purchases "without significantly impacting current year collections" (10-K page:55); that is a management statement, not evidenced by the supplied tables.

- Earnings quality. In Q2 2026 changes in expected recoveries were 96,924 of income from operations of 153,282, driven by the European forecast revision. These are estimates of future collections recognised in income now; Portfolio income, which the filing calls the more predictable yield component, was 267,799 (Q2 10-Q page:29). Cash collections of 558,545 are the stronger measure of performance in the quarter.

- Liquidity. Cash is 132,431 against total availability of 998,468, of which 733,096 is based on current ERC. Availability moved from 1,099,466 at December 31, 2025 to 998,468 at June 30, 2026 as revolver drawings rose; the supplied text does not give letters of credit drawn.

- Maturities. After the April 2026 extension no principal other than the term loan's quarterly payments falls due before February 2028 (Q2 10-Q page:42). The 2029 concentration is the largest, with both revolvers, the 2029 notes and the term loan balance maturing in October 2029.

- Interest. Interest expense, net was 251,788 in FY2025 (cash interest paid 259,061) and 127,881 in H1 2026. Interest expense, net rose 3.2% year on year in Q2 2026, which the filing attributes primarily to higher average debt balances (Q2 10-Q page:32).
## Calculations
All inputs are in thousands of USD unless stated. Results are calculated here and are not issuer-printed unless said.
### C1 and C2: gross and net debt over Adjusted EBITDA
Gross = debt principal / Adjusted EBITDA. Net = (debt principal − cash and cash equivalents) / Adjusted EBITDA.
| Period | Debt principal | Cash | Adjusted EBITDA | Gross (x) | Net debt | Net (x) |
### C3 and C4: derived cash interest and interest cover
Last-twelve-months cash interest = FY2025 cash paid for interest − prior-year-to-date + current-year-to-date.
### C5: tie-outs of printed totals
- Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation columns sum to the printed totals: FY2024 1,137,552; FY2025 1,315,474; LTM Mar 31, 2026 1,348,599; LTM Jun 30, 2026 1,358,913 (components in the table above).
- Last-twelve-months net loss to June 30, 2026: (305,142) − 46,033 + 86,127 = (265,048), which equals the printed figure (Q2 10-Q page:25 and page:36).
- Growth in last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA: 1,358,913 / 1,240,092 − 1 = 9.58%, which matches the printed 9.6% (page:25).

- Availability at June 30, 2026 equals committed less outstanding for each revolving facility (1,075,000 − 565,092 = 509,908; 873,733 − 618,227 = 255,506; 725,000 − 491,946 = 233,054) and the sum 998,468 equals the printed total. The ERC-based parts sum to 733,096 and the additional parts to 265,372. The same holds at March 31, 2026 (995,995) and December 31, 2025 (1,099,466).
- Principal of credit facilities and senior notes at June 30, 2026: 2,130,621 + 1,640,630 = 3,771,251; less 11,898 gives 3,759,353, the balance sheet figure.
### C6: liquidity
| Date | Cash | Total availability | Cash plus availability |

Letters of credit drawn are Not supplied, so no deduction is made. No facility is described as expiring within twelve months of June 30, 2026 in the supplied text; the earliest revolver maturity is October 2029 (Q2 10-Q page:11).
### C7: derived maturity schedule at June 30, 2026

Inputs from Q2 10-Q page:11 and page:42 and 10-K page:87 to page:92. Term loan balance 455,111 less 2.5 million quarterly payments: H2 2026 = 2 × 2,500 = 5,000; 2027 = 4 × 2,500 = 10,000; 2028 = 10,000; remainder at October 28, 2029 = 455,111 − 5,000 − 10,000 − 10,000 = 430,111.

Cross-check against the 10-K schedule at December 31, 2025 (page:86): 2028 = 398,000 + 10,000 + 2,611 = 410,611, which equals the printed 410,611; 2029 = 520,736 + 499,848 + 350,000 + 430,111 = 1,800,695, which equals the printed figure. The 10-K 2027 figure of 587,335 included the European facility 577,335 plus 10,000 and is superseded for that facility by the extension to April 30, 2031.
### C8: illustrative cash bridge (not an issuer measure)
Adjusted EBITDA − cash paid for interest − cash paid for income taxes − purchases of nonperforming loan portfolios − purchases of property and equipment.

Net debt cash flows, from the cash flow statement (10-K page:71): FY2025 1,203,549 − 1,291,725 − 10,000 + 351,990 = 253,814 (lines of credit proceeds less payments, less long-term debt payments, plus senior notes proceeds); FY2024 1,901,645 − 1,720,836 + 472,611 − 445,000 + 555,438 − 298,000 = 465,858. FY2024 also had a 59,848 net increase in interest-bearing deposits and FY2025 an 88,193 net decrease. Adjusted EBITDA includes the noncontrolling interests' share and the bridge excludes distributions to noncontrolling interests (25,132 in FY2025), share repurchases (20,000 in FY2025) and fees, so the shortfall to be financed is larger than shown.
### C9: other ratios

- Change in debt principal from December 31, 2024 to June 30, 2026: 3,771,251 − 3,337,541 = 433,710, which is 13.0% of 3,337,541. Change in Adjusted EBITDA from FY2024 to the last twelve months to June 30, 2026: 1,358,913 / 1,137,552 − 1 = 19.5%.
- Share of income from operations: changes in expected recoveries 96,924 / 153,282 = 63.2% in Q2 2026; 140,810 / 256,536 = 54.9% in H1 2026.
- Adjusted EBITDA less cash receipts less Adjusted operating expenses, FY2025: 1,315,474 − 1,298,123 = 17,351.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| PRA Group is a widely held, listed buyer and collector of nonperforming loans with no sponsor or pending ownership change in the sources. Credit relevance centres on estimate-driven ERC, a 54.0% European weighting and debt-funded purchasing. | Medium | Seller concentration, executed debt documents and the proxy statement are not supplied, and nothing after August 7, 2026 is covered. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| No sponsor, controlling holder or pending transaction appears in the sources; there were 44 holders of record, and no dividends were paid in the three years to 2025. | Creditor alignment rests on public-company capital allocation, mainly repurchases, and not on sponsor behaviour. | Medium |

| Europe holds 54.0% of ERC, and the European facility was extended to April 30, 2031 with the maximum ERC ratio cut from 45.0% to 40.0%. | Refinancing risk on the largest drawn credit facility falls, but currency and fragmented regulation concentrate exposure. | Medium |

| The June 2026 European forecast review raised European ERC by $348.5 million; management links it to six years of cash overperformance. | ERC and ERC-based availability rest on model forecasts, so revisions can move both earnings and borrowing capacity. | Medium |

| A new CEO in 2025 led to a two-segment structure, cost reductions and call-centre consolidation, while U.S. legal collection expenses rose ahead of collections. | Margins depend on the cost plan outrunning higher upfront legal spend. | Medium |

| A $150 million share repurchase program was approved on August 3, 2026, after $20.0 million of repurchases in the first half of 2026. | Equity returns compete with debt reduction while purchases are debt funded; covenants cap capacity. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

PRA Group, Inc. is a Delaware specialty finance company headquartered in Norfolk, Virginia that buys nonperforming consumer loans from banks, consumer finance companies, auto finance providers and other creditors, and collects on them over several years through call centers, external vendors, legal recovery and digital channels (10-K page:6 to page:8). It reports two segments, the U.S. and Europe, created in Q4 2025 after a new chief executive officer was appointed in 2025 (10-K page:103), plus smaller operations in South America, Canada and Australia. Revenue is accrued from the expected collections of each portfolio, so reported profit depends on management's collection forecasts; the filing itself calls Portfolio income the more predictable component and Changes in expected recoveries the estimate-driven one (Q2 10-Q page:29). The company is publicly listed with 44 holders of record and no sponsor, parent or controlling holder is disclosed in the supplied sources; the proxy statement that would give beneficial ownership is not supplied. No acquisition, take-private or other ownership transaction is described in the supplied sources. The transactions that are described are financing and portfolio events: the September 30, 2025 issue of euro-denominated 6.250% senior notes due 2032 by a Luxembourg subsidiary, the April 30, 2026 amendment and extension of the European revolving credit facility, the April 2025 sale of an 11.7% interest in a Brazilian servicing company, and the August 3, 2026 approval of a new share repurchase program. Creditor-relevant change is concentrated in three areas: the June 30, 2026 European forecast review that raised European ERC by $348.5 million; the cost and organisation programme under the "PRA 3.0" strategy (management's term); and capital returns through repurchases while portfolio purchases are financed with debt. Documented actions show no priming, uptiering, drop-down or related-party leakage, but the legal capacity under the credit agreements and indentures cannot be assessed because those documents are not supplied.
### Company and operating model

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, take-private, merger or other ownership transaction is described in the supplied sources, and the context holds no deal terms, so the transaction view is Insufficient Information for any pending or announced ownership event as of 2026-11-05; the sources end on August 7, 2026. The financing and portfolio transactions that are described are as follows. On September 30, 2025 the company completed a private offering of EUR 300.0 million (US$352.4 million at issuance) of 6.250% senior notes due September 30, 2032 through its wholly owned subsidiary PRA Group Europe Holding II S.à r.l.; the notes are senior unsecured obligations of that issuer, guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by PRA Group, Inc. and by the domestic restricted subsidiaries that guarantee the North American facility, with interest payable on March 31 and September 30, a change of control put at 101%, and a call schedule at 103.125% from September 30, 2028 falling to par from 2030 (10-K page:90). The use of proceeds is not stated in the pages read, so it is Insufficient Information; the cash flow statement shows the proceeds within financing activities (10-K page:71) and the company describes the issue as its first euro-denominated senior notes (10-K page:38). On April 30, 2026 the company amended and restated its European revolving credit facility: the maturity moved from November 23, 2027 to April 30, 2031, the maximum ERC ratio fell from 45.0% to 40.0%, and, subject to conditions, borrowers may make investments in or loans to joint ventures up to EUR 100 million; the Q1 2026 10-Q reports the aggregate revolving borrowings available and funding costs as unchanged (Q1 10-Q page:17; Q2 10-Q page:11). The new program follows repurchases of $20.0 million in 2025 and $20.0 million in the first half of 2026 (10-K page:38; Q2 10-Q page:15). | Reporting: reconciliations of non-GAAP measures, ERC by year and quarterly disclosure of forecast revisions | Supportive (transparent reporting) | Allows creditors to track ERC revisions and Adjusted EBITDA; the revision explanation is management's | None | High |

| No priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release is described in the supplied sources | Insufficient Information | Absence in summary disclosures is not evidence of absence; the governing documents are missing | Capacity not assessable | Insufficient |
### Evidence-to-implication translations
| Theme | Evidence | Risk mechanic | Credit implication | Countering conflict or limit |

| Revenue durability | Q2 10-Q page:9: forecasts for the majority of European pools were updated, giving a positive adjustment to changes in expected future recoveries of approximately $105 million, "partially offset" by lower forecasts on other pools | Revenue recognised from forecast revisions is an estimate of future cash; a reversal would reduce revenue and, through the ERC-based borrowing base, availability | Earnings and liquidity are sensitive to model accuracy; the cash collection trend in CP-1 is the cross-check | The release says the change in expected recoveries was "primarily driven by" the approximately $349 million ERC increase; the filing puts the income adjustment near $105 million. Different measures, not a numeric conflict |

| Margin and cash-flow risk | U.S. legal collection expenses rose 40.6% in Q2 2026 and U.S. compensation fell 13.7% (Q2 10-Q page:33) | Legal recovery costs are incurred before collections; a slower court process leaves cost without cash | Margin recovery in the U.S. depends on legal channel productivity; U.S. adjusted segment operating income was flat year on year in Q2 2026 (17,315 against 17,511 in thousands, Q2 10-Q page:33) | Management expects the legal spend to support future collections growth (Q2 release page:3), a Management Language claim |

| Concentration | Europe is 54.0% of ERC; the largest drawn credit facility is European; seller concentration is not disclosed | Currency moves and national regulation change collections and debt in the same currencies; the euro notes and European facility partly match the euro assets | Concentration is geographic and regulatory; the natural hedge is partial and not quantified in the sources | Seller concentration is Insufficient Information |

| Ownership alignment | Public company, no sponsor; repurchases and a new program; no dividends | Equity returns come from repurchases that compete with debt reduction | Alignment with creditors depends on leverage tolerance; no sponsor extraction behaviour is documented | Covenant capacity for repurchases and the indenture baskets are not supplied |

| Funding and refinancing | European facility extended to April 30, 2031; the next revolver maturities are October 2029 (CP-1) | Longer maturities lower rollover risk in the nearer years; 2029 holds the largest cluster in CP-1 | Refinancing sensitivity moves to 2029; ERC-based availability can change with revisions | Amended agreement not supplied |

| Key uncertainties | Covenant ratio levels are not printed; multi-state Attorneys General matter unresolved; CFPB direction uncertain per the 10-K | Unobserved headroom plus a possible cash settlement | Monitoring posture rather than a conclusion | Exact accrual not stated in the pages read |
### Conflicts
No factual conflict between sources was found that requires logging unreconciled. Two differences were checked and are not conflicts:

- European facility maturity: the 10-K states November 23, 2027 (page:89) and the Q2 10-Q states April 30, 2031 (page:11). The second follows an amendment dated April 30, 2026 (Q1 10-Q page:17), so they are sequential, not contradictory.

- European review size: the Q2 release speaks of an approximately $349 million ERC increase driving the rise in changes in expected recoveries (page:3), while the Q2 10-Q gives $348.5 million for the ERC increase (page:24) and approximately $105 million as the positive adjustment to changes in expected future recoveries (page:9). Different measures; a consumer must not treat the ERC increase as income.

| Add-back bridge for covenant EBITDA | High | The issuer's Adjusted EBITDA is not the covenant measure | Supply credit agreement definitions |
| Events after August 7, 2026 | Medium | Financing, ratings and the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | Supply later filings |

| CP-2 | Ready with limitations | Business model and estimate-driven revenue, Europe weighting, funding model, the European facility amendment, repurchase behaviour, regulatory and litigation exposure | Frames which financial risks are structural and which are estimate-driven | Executed documents, covenant levels, seller concentration, ownership detail | Carry the gaps as restrictions; do not infer legal capacity |

## Calculations

No new calculation. Percentages quoted (40.6% and 13.7% change in U.S. legal collection expenses and compensation, 40.4% and 54.0% of ERC, 103.625% issue price) are as printed in the cited pages. Financial amounts are those in the CP-1 handoff.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The fundamental credit view is adequate and stable: gross debt is 2.78x issuer Adjusted EBITDA and cash interest is covered 5.36x, but earnings, ERC and ERC-linked availability rest on internal forecasts, and purchases are debt funded. | Medium | Covenant ratios and executed debt documents are not supplied, and nothing after August 7, 2026 is covered, so headroom and the current position are unobserved. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Gross debt of USD 3,771.3 million is 2.78x last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA, and cash interest is covered 5.36x. | Leverage and cover are moderate on the issuer's own measure, which adds back collections applied to principal. | Medium |

| Liquidity is USD 132.4 million of cash plus USD 998.5 million of availability, of which USD 733.1 million depends on current ERC. | Liquidity covers the estimated next 12 months of interest, fees and principal 4.57x, but shrinks if ERC forecasts are cut. | Medium |

| No principal other than term loan payments falls due before February 2028, and 48.7% of principal falls due in 2029. | Near-term rollover risk is low; refinancing risk concentrates in 2029. | Medium |

| Portfolio purchases exceeded Adjusted EBITDA after cash interest and taxes by USD 190.7 million in FY2025 and USD 502.9 million in FY2024. | Leverage will drift up unless purchases slow or collections grow faster than the spend. | Medium |

| Secured credit facilities are 56.5% of debt principal and the senior notes are unsecured. | Noteholders rank behind secured lenders on the collateral; guarantor coverage of European assets is not evidenced. | Medium |
### Credit view

PRA Group's fundamental credit is adequate and stable, with moderate leverage that depends on forecast accuracy more than on a cash buffer. The strongest support is cash earning power: last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,358.9 million covers cash interest of USD 253.4 million 5.36x, gross debt is 2.78x that EBITDA, and no principal other than term loan payments is due before February 2028. The weakest point is that revenue, ERC and ERC-linked availability of USD 998.5 million all rest on internal collection forecasts, while purchases have exceeded post-interest cash earnings in each of the last two years. What decides the outcome is whether collections keep matching forecasts and whether purchasing is held to the cash the business generates. Covenant headroom cannot be observed.
### Key findings

First, the leverage and coverage position is moderate and has improved. Gross debt over Adjusted EBITDA was 2.93x in FY2024 and 2.78x for the last twelve months to June 30, 2026, because between FY2024 and the last twelve months to June 30, 2026 Adjusted EBITDA rose 19.5% while debt principal rose 13.0%. Cash interest cover was 5.08x in FY2025 and 5.36x for the last twelve months [CP-1 leverage and interest cover tables]. The measure is the issuer's own non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA, which adds back collections applied to principal, so it is a cash-collections measure and is not the covenant definition; ratios should not be compared with the 3.50x and 2.50x limits.

Second, reported profit is more estimate-driven than cash. In Q2 2026 changes in expected recoveries were USD 96.9 million of USD 153.3 million income from operations, after a European forecast review raised European ERC by USD 348.5 million and added approximately USD 105 million to changes in expected future recoveries [CP-1; CP-1A revenue model row; Q2 10-Q page:9]. The USD 348.5 million is an ERC change and not income. Cash collections of USD 558.5 million in the quarter are the firmer measure.

Third, liquidity depends on the borrowing base. Cash is USD 132.4 million against availability of USD 998.5 million, of which USD 733.1 million, 73.4%, is based on current ERC at advance rates of 35% for Core and 55% for Insolvency pools [CP-1 liquidity tables; 10-K page:87]. A downward ERC revision would cut capacity at the moment it is most needed. Cash and availability total USD 1,130.9 million, 4.57x the USD 247.7 million of interest, unused fees and principal payments the company estimates for the next 12 months (Q2 10-Q page:42).

Fourth, purchasing, not operations, drives the debt trend. Adjusted EBITDA after cash interest, cash taxes and capital expenditure was short of cash spent on portfolio purchases by USD 190.7 million in FY2025 and USD 502.9 million in FY2024 [CP-1 bridge]. Borrowings rose in both years. Management says it can slow purchases without hurting current-year collections (10-K page:55), which is a management claim, but forward flow agreements carry few minimum obligations [CP-1A operating model], so the lever exists in the documents.

Fifth, refinancing risk is deferred and then concentrated. The European revolving facility now matures on April 30, 2031, the 2028 senior notes of USD 398.0 million fall due on February 1, 2028 (about 15 months after the as-of date), and USD 1,837.1 million, 48.7% of principal, matures in 2029 across both other revolvers, the 2029 notes and the term loan [CP-1 maturity table].

Sixth, structure and visibility are unresolved. Credit facilities of USD 2,130.6 million, 56.5% of principal, are secured by liens on U.S. and UK assets and on European subsidiary equity, and the USD 1,640.6 million of senior notes are unsecured [CP-1 debt table; 10-K page:87 to page:92]. About 60% of debt is fixed or hedged, and a 50 basis point move changes annual interest by an estimated USD 7.8 million (Q2 10-Q page:46). The notes' guarantor structure, the credit agreement definitions and the covenant ratios are not supplied.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The company has a long-dated, diversified liability stack: secured revolving facilities in several currencies, a term loan and unsecured notes, with no principal beyond term loan payments due for about 15 months and revolvers running to 2029 and 2031. Cash earning power is growing: cash collections of USD 558.5 million in Q2 2026 are 4.2% above Q2 2025, ERC is USD 8,894.5 million, 2.36x debt principal, and Adjusted EBITDA has risen 9.6% year on year. Purchasing is discretionary, which gives management a lever over debt growth. The European business is organised so that portfolio ownership and collections sit in the same entity, and the European and UK facilities are multi-currency to match funding by currency (10-K page:65). The company is widely held, with no sponsor, no dividends in three years and a documented early extension of its European facility, and it discloses reconciliations of its non-GAAP measures and ERC revisions.

Weaknesses. Earnings, ERC and the ERC-based part of availability depend on internal models and forecasts, and a USD 412.6 million goodwill impairment in Q3 2025 shows that valuations can reset sharply. Cash on hand is small, USD 132.4 million against USD 3,771.3 million of debt, so liquidity is a function of revolver access and covenant compliance, which cannot be observed. Debt has grown faster than cash after purchases in two consecutive years, and shareholder returns continue through repurchases, with a USD 150 million program approved on August 3, 2026. Europe is 54.0% of ERC, adding currency and fragmented regulatory exposure, and the U.S. segment's adjusted operating income was flat year on year in Q2 2026 as legal collection spending rose. A multi-state Attorneys General investigation open since 2015 remains unresolved. The 2029 maturity cluster and the structural position of unsecured noteholders behind secured facilities add refinancing and ranking sensitivity.
### Credit assessment
| Dimension | Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Overall fundamental view | Adequate and stable, with estimate risk and unobserved covenant headroom | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, cover and liquidity tables; CP-1A company and operating model and governance tables |

| Business risk | Moderate: recurring portfolio purchasing with multi-year collection, but revenue is forecast-based and Europe-weighted | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A revenue model, geography and supply rows |

| Financial risk | Moderate: gross debt 2.78x and cash interest cover 5.36x on the issuer's own EBITDA | Documentary Fact for the ratios; Analyst Interpretation for the label | Medium | CP-1 calculations C1 to C4 |
| Liquidity | Adequate for 12 months, dependent on ERC-linked availability | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 liquidity table; Q2 10-Q page:42 |
| Refinancing | Low before 2028; concentrated in 2029 | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 maturity table |
| Governance and capital allocation | Neutral or Mixed: repurchases alongside debt-funded purchasing; no extraction documented | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A governance table |
| Covenant headroom | Not assessable: ratio levels and definitions not supplied | Insufficient Information | Not assessable | CP-1 covenant table; CP-1A monitoring gaps |
### Thesis

PRA Group is an adequately financed, moderately levered collector of nonperforming loans whose debt service is supported by growing cash collections but whose reported earnings, ERC and ERC-linked liquidity rest on internal forecasts and whose debt keeps rising to fund portfolio purchases.
### Basis register for strengths and weaknesses
| Item | Type | Category | Basis |
| Long-dated diversified funding with no principal before February 2028 other than term loan payments | Strength | Documentary Fact | CP-1 debt and maturity tables; Q2 10-Q page:42 |
| Growing cash collections, ERC and Adjusted EBITDA | Strength | Documentary Fact | CP-1 financial table and leverage calculations |
| Discretionary purchasing | Strength | Documentary Fact | CP-1A supply row; Q2 10-Q page:17 |
| Management states it can slow purchases without hurting current-year collections | Strength (claim) | Management Language | 10-K page:55 |
| Currency matching through multi-currency facilities | Strength | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:65 |
| Forecast-dependent earnings, ERC and availability | Weakness | Documentary Fact | CP-1A revenue model row; Q2 10-Q page:9 |
| Thin cash against debt | Weakness | Documentary Fact | CP-1 liquidity table |
| Purchases above post-interest cash earnings; debt growth | Weakness | Documentary Fact | CP-1 calculation C8 |
| Europe weighting of ERC | Weakness | Documentary Fact | CP-1A geography row |
| Unsecured notes behind secured facilities | Weakness | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 debt table; 10-K page:87 to page:92 |
| Covenant headroom unobservable | Weakness | Insufficient Information | CP-1 covenant table |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Forecast reversal | A downward ERC or collection forecast revision lowers revenue and, through the 35% and 55% advance rates, borrowing base availability together | Earnings and liquidity weaken at once; leverage on cash-based EBITDA rises only if collections also fall | Material | CP-1 liquidity table; CP-1A revenue model row |

| Debt-funded purchasing | Purchases exceed post-interest cash earnings; deficit is funded by borrowing | Leverage drifts up if collections growth slows; monitor debt over EBITDA each quarter | Material | CP-1 calculation C8 |

| Covenant opacity | Total leverage, senior secured leverage, fixed charge and ERC ratio tests exist but levels and definitions are not supplied; the European ERC ratio cap fell to 40.0% | Headroom cannot be observed; a breach would restrict drawing and distributions | Material | CP-1 covenant table; CP-1A timeline |

| 2029 maturity cluster | Both other revolvers, the 2029 notes and the term loan mature within a short window in 2029 | Refinancing must succeed in one period; market access matters | Material | CP-1 maturity table |

| Europe and currency | 54.0% of ERC is in Europe; euro and sterling assets and liabilities move with exchange rates; regulation is fragmented | Translation and conversion effects change debt and ERC; matching is partial and not quantified | Material | CP-1A geography row; 10-K page:65 |

| Structural ranking | Secured facilities of USD 2,130.6 million have first claim on pledged assets and subsidiary equity; the notes are unsecured | Noteholders' position depends on collateral value and guarantor reach, which are not evidenced | Material | CP-1 debt table |

| Regulatory and litigation | CFPB supervision, multi-state Attorneys General matter since 2015 with an accrual of undisclosed amount | A settlement or practice change could cost cash and slow collections | Material | CP-1A operating model row |

| Shareholder returns | Repurchases of USD 20.0 million in the first half of 2026 and a USD 150 million program | Competes with debt reduction while purchases are debt funded; covenant baskets cap it | Minor | CP-1A governance table |
| Floating rate exposure | About 40% of debt is not fixed or hedged; 50 basis points is about USD 7.8 million per year | Modest next to cash interest of USD 253.4 million | Minor | Q2 10-Q page:46 |
### Checks against the filings and the upstream handoffs
| Check | Result |

| Gross and net leverage and cover recomputed from CP-1 inputs (debt principal USD 3,771.3 million, cash USD 132.4 million, Adjusted EBITDA USD 1,358.9 million, cash interest USD 253.4 million) | 2.78x, 2.68x and 5.36x, as in CP-1 |
| Availability USD 998.5 million equals the sum of committed less drawn on the three revolvers (Q2 10-Q page:40 and page:41) | Agrees |
| Interest rate mix and sensitivity (Q2 10-Q page:46) and next 12 months obligations (page:42) | Opened; used in findings above |
| Foreign exchange mitigation (10-K page:65) | Opened; used as a strength |
| Corrections to upstream handoffs | None found. CP-1A's characterisation of the European review as ERC, not income, is retained and applied here |
## Calculations
Inputs are from the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs and the cited pages, in thousands of USD unless stated.

- K1, maturity concentration: 2029 principal 1,837,149 / 3,771,251 = 48.7%. Principal due by end-2028: 5,000 + 10,000 + 408,245 = 423,245; 423,245 / 3,771,251 = 11.2%. The 2028 notes mature on February 1, 2028, 453 days after the as-of date of 2026-11-05 (about 14.9 months); the October 28, 2029 revolver maturity is 1,088 days after it (about 3.0 years).

- K2, secured share: credit facility borrowings 2,130,621 / 3,771,251 = 56.5%; senior notes 1,640,630 / 3,771,251 = 43.5%. Whether the Colombian facility (245) is secured is not stated and is immaterial to the share.
- K3, ERC-based share of availability: 733,096 / 998,468 = 73.4%.

- K4, liquidity cover of the next 12 months: cash 132,431 + availability 998,468 = 1,130,899; divided by the printed estimate of interest, unused fees and principal payments for the next 12 months of 247,700 (Q2 10-Q page:42) = 4.57x. Availability alone: 998,468 / 247,700 = 4.03x. Letters of credit drawn are Not supplied, so no deduction is made.
- K5, interest rate sensitivity: 7,800 / 253,430 (cash interest, CP-1 C4) = 3.1% of cash interest per 50 basis points, on the company's estimate (Q2 10-Q page:46).

- K6, illustrative cost-adjusted ERC cover (analyst construct, not an issuer measure): ERC 8,894,515 x Q2 2026 cash efficiency ratio 61.2% (Q2 10-Q page:25) = 5,443,443; divided by debt principal 3,771,251 = 1.44x. ERC is undiscounted, before interest and taxes, and assumes the cost ratio persists; the result is a sensitivity and not a coverage test.

- K7, growth rates used in findings: debt principal 3,771,251 / 3,337,541 − 1 = 13.0%; Adjusted EBITDA 1,358,913 / 1,137,552 − 1 = 19.5% (CP-1 C9). Cash collections 558,545 / 536,288 − 1 = 4.2%, matching the printed 4.2% (Q2 10-Q page:25).

- K8, funding shortfall after cash interest, taxes and capital expenditure: FY2025 −190,676 and FY2024 −502,881 (CP-1 C8, recomputed: 1,315,474 − 259,061 − 38,528 − 1,203,740 − 4,821 and 1,137,552 − 224,099 − 5,222 − 1,407,067 − 4,045).
- K9, share of income from operations: 96,924 / 153,282 = 63.2% (CP-1 C9).
## Gaps
| Gap | What it affects | Severity | Action |

| Covenant ratio levels and covenant EBITDA definition not supplied | Headroom, distribution capacity, drawing conditions; confidence capped below High | High | Supply the executed credit agreements and compliance certificates |

| Executed credit agreements and indentures, including the amended European agreement, not supplied (inherited from CP-0 and CP-1A) | Legal capacity, guarantor reach, ranking and the joint venture investment basket | High | Supply the documents |
| Nothing after August 7, 2026, including any report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | Current leverage, liquidity and ERC at the as-of date | Medium | Supply later filings or confirm none |
| Letters of credit drawn, and the maturity of interest-bearing deposits of USD 100.5 million | Liquidity net of usage, debt perimeter | Medium | Supply usage and deposit detail |
| Seller concentration, accrued amount for the Attorneys General matter, use of proceeds of the 2032 notes | Supply and litigation risk | Medium | Supply if disclosed |
| Ratings, market prices and valuation inputs | Market view | Low | Not required for this module |
| Proxy statement | Ownership and governance detail | Low | Supply if governance scoring is needed |
## Next module

CP-5: trace the figures in the Key findings and Calculations to their CP-1 tables and cited pages; check that every statement about covenant limits is framed as not comparable to the Adjusted EBITDA ratios; check that the European ERC increase is never presented as income; and treat the cost-adjusted ERC cover (K6) and the secured share (K2) as analyst constructs.

### Evidence trace view

The credit work for PRA Group is traceable enough for committee use with restrictions, because every headline figure rests on filed statements and recomputes exactly. The strongest support is that leverage, cover, liquidity and maturity numbers all agree with printed inputs, and management claims are tagged as management language rather than fact. The weakest point is that no executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied, so covenant headroom, ranking and guarantor statements rest on filing summaries and cannot be traced to primary legal text. The outcome turns on whether those documents and any report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 can be obtained; until then conclusions that depend on them stay restricted. One material framing defect and six minor defects are logged for correction.
### Traceability conclusion

Scope and method. Every numeric claim in the Reader summary rows and key tables of CP-1, CP-1A and CP-2 was opened at its cited page or located on a neighbouring page of the same source; every number in the CP-1 financial table was checked against the cited statements by search; and every derived figure (CP-1 C1 to C9, CP-2 K1 to K9) was recomputed from its printed inputs. Narrative sentences were traced where they carry a number, a date or a legal characterisation. Prose without figures (for example descriptive business text) was sampled and not exhaustively traced.

Result. No unsupported headline claim, no figure without a source and no arithmetic error was found. Identity, as-of date and source hashes in the upstream handoffs match the run. Management characterisations ("record ERC levels", competitive strengths, ability to slow purchases) are tagged Management Language. Two analyst constructs (illustrative cash bridge, cost-adjusted ERC cover) are labelled as such. Confidence score and band are not computed here because the scoring script is not available in this host run; the Medium confidence stated is a judgment.

First, reframe the structural ranking statement in CP-2 (issue I3) as an Analyst Interpretation resting on filing summaries, and obtain the executed credit agreements, security documents and indentures; this removes the only material defect and lifts the legal restriction. Second, correct the two CP-1 wording and locator points (I1, I2) and the CP-2 generalisation of advance rates (I4). Third, confirm the Colombian facility maturity and security (I5, I6) and qualify "stable" (I7). Fourth, obtain any filing after August 7, 2026, including the report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, and refresh leverage, liquidity and ERC.

Committee status: Restricted. The fundamental credit view and the financial base may be used, with the stated definition limits, as a view on data to June 30, 2026. Conclusions on covenant headroom, ranking, guarantor reach and legal capacity may not be used until the executed documents are traced. Research QA status: Restricted.
